title: The Drove Road

where.detail: a shepherds' fold on the drove road round the north shore of the tarn, across the water from Coldmere

time: the first day off the mountain, from the first miles to dusk
last_beat: Across the tarn the column's fires came out on Coldmere's green, and Rae pointed with the goad at the biggest light, her uncle's inn, where he would be pouring for them.

people.did: Walked the first miles at Hob's head to Maelis's stone, watching every rise for the banner; knew Aldric at the head of the column and wanted to stand on the Holloway and meet him; owned that he had decided before anyone spoke, and gave Rae the road.
people.now: At a shepherds' fold on the drove road round the tarn, with the company, the column's fires across the water at Coldmere.

facts.fact: He walked the first miles of the Holloway at the ox's head, the stick in one hand.
facts.evidence: So he walked at Hob's head with one hand on the yoke and the stick in the other

facts.fact: He owned that he had decided to meet the banner before anyone spoke, and left the road to Rae.
He knew Aldric at the head of the column by his seat on a horse.

people.did: Told him she had told the mare her name; took the cart off the Holloway onto the drove road round the tarn rather than drive it into a Lance on the march, and argued it out loud; waited for his word before she drove on.
people.now: At the fold on the north shore of the tarn, looking across at Coldmere, where the column has stopped on the green and her uncle keeps the inn at the water's edge.

facts.fact: She told the grey mare her name at the dealer's, as she said she would.
facts.evidence: In her ear, at the dealer's, the morning I went down.

facts.fact: She would not drive her cart into a Lance on the march: a Lance on the march takes a cart.
facts.evidence: This is my road, and I'm not driving it into him so you can see his face.

facts.fact: Her uncle keeps the inn whose light is the biggest in Coldmere, at the water's edge.

people.did: Rode the tailboard, ordered that sheep not be counted separately, backed the carter, and called the fold the finest inn in the Lowmarch.
people.now: At the fold on the drove road, asking where they keep the beer.

facts.fact: He backed the carter over the banner: a Lance's outriders have eyes.
facts.evidence: but they've outriders, and outriders have eyes

people.did: Let him walk to the next milestone and no further, then put him back on the tailboard.
people.now: With the company at the fold on the drove road.

facts.fact: She let him walk the Holloway to a milestone, then had him ride.
facts.evidence: To the next stone. Then you ride, and you don't argue.

people.did: Counted everything on the road, sheep included until Hollis forbade it; counted the column at forty-six and its cart; began to count the stars.
people.now: Flat on her back on the cart at the fold, counting the sky.

facts.fact: She counted the column on the Holloway: forty-six riders and the Confessor's cart.
On the mountain the sky had mostly been cloud; at the fold she began to count the stars.

people.did: Ranged ahead on the road and came back twice to report nothing.
people.now: With the company at the fold on the drove road.

codex.name: The drove road
codex.text: A walled track that leaves the Holloway above Coldmere and runs north round the far side of the tarn: the carter's road round a Lance on the march (Ch 5 Sc 1).

fired.evidence: In her ear, at the dealer's, the morning I went down.

season: clear cold after the first snow, on the road below the mountain

now.against: A Lance on the march and the Confessor's cart, camped on Coldmere's green across the tarn.
now.next: Round the tarn by the drove road, to come at Coldmere from the north.

title: Across the Water

where.detail: on the fold wall above the tarn at the shepherds' fold, across the water from Coldmere

time: the first night off the mountain, after dark
last_beat: Her shoulder stayed against his, and, looking across the water and not at him, Rae asked her one question of the night: what he had been going to say to Aldric on the road.

people.did: Took Rae a cup from the kettle on the fold wall with no light, asked about the man pouring for the column, would not tell her it would be all right, and offered to go round Coldmere rather than put her uncle to it.
people.now: On the fold wall beside Rae, with Ash across their feet, her question waiting: what he was going to say to Aldric.

facts.fact: He told Rae they would go round Coldmere rather than put her uncle to it.
facts.evidence: If it isn't good for the inn,

people.did: Kept the fold dark from the far shore; told him about her uncle and his taproom, and that she went out the back the night the list was read without asking him; made her one question of the night his: what he was going to say to Aldric.
people.now: On the fold wall above the tarn, watching her uncle's door across the water, her shoulder against Darrow's.

facts.fact: Her uncle keeps the only inn in Coldmere; everything on the Holloway goes through his taproom, and he pours for all of them and forgets none of it.
facts.evidence: He pours for all of them, and he listens to all of them, and he forgets none of it.

facts.fact: Her uncle poured for the reader the night the list was read in his taproom, between the names.
facts.evidence: filled the reader's cup between the names

facts.fact: The night the list was read she went out the back to the House's cart without asking her uncle, the first thing she had not asked him.
facts.evidence: That was the first thing I didn't.

facts.fact: She does not know whether her uncle will give them up: he does what is good for the inn.
facts.evidence: He'll do what's good for the inn. He always has.

people.did: Built the fire inside the shepherds' hut so it would not show across the tarn, on Rae's word.
people.now: In the shepherds' hut with the kettle.

people.did: Lay down across Darrow's and Rae's feet on the fold wall.
people.now: Across their feet on the fold wall.

now.against: A Lance and the Confessor's cart camped on Coldmere's green; her uncle pouring for them.
now.next: Round the tarn by the drove road.
